Short title extent and commencement

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER I.‑PRELIMINARY
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑This Ordinance may be called the West Pakistan Primary
Education Ordinance, 1962.
(2) It extends to the whole of
the Province of West Pakistan except the Special Areas.
(3) This section and section 2
shall come into force at once and such other provisions of the Ordinance shall
come into force in such areas and on such dates as the Government may, by
notification in the official Gazette, specify in this behalf.

Definitions

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER I.‑PRELIMINARY
2. Definitions.‑In this
Ordinance, unless the context otherwise requires, the following expressions
shall have the meanings hereby respectively assigned to them, that is to say‑
(a) "area of
compulsion" means the area in which primary education is compulsory ;
(b) "child" means a
child of either sex, whose age at the beginning of the school year is not less
than five years and not more than fourteen years ;
(c) "District" means
a District as defined is the Basic Democracies Order, 1959 (P. 0. No. 18 of
1959) ;
(d) "Government"
means the Government of West Pakistan;
(e) "Government primary
school" means a primary school maintained by Government;
(f) "local area"
means a local area as defined in the Basic Democracies Order, 1959 (P. O. No.
18 of 1)59)
(g) "local council"
means a local council constituted under the Basic Democracies Order, 1959 (P.
O. No. 18 of 1959) ;
(h) "parent" includes
a guardian or any person who has the custody of a child;
(i) "prescribed"
means prescribed by rules made under this Ordinance;
(j) "primary
education" means education pertaining to all or any of the Classes. I to
VIII, in any school other than a High School;
(k) "primary school"
means a school, other than a High School, in which primary education is
imparted ;
(1) "recognised
school" means a school or department of a school recognised by Government
as suitable for imparting primary education and includes, for the purposes of
Chapter IV, a High School.
(2) Any other expression used
in this Ordinance with reference to the Basic Democracies Order, 1959 (P. O.
Order No. 18 of 1959) or the Municipal Administration Ordinance, 1960
(Ordinance X of 1960) shall have the meanings assigned to it in the said Order
or the said Ordinance, as the case may be.

Repeal and savings

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER I.‑PRELIMINARY
3. Repeal and savings.‑On
the coming into force of this Ordinance in any area, the enactments mentioned
in the Schedule shall, if and in so far as applicable to that area, stand
repealed;
Provided, that where any
educational institution has been excepted from the operation of this Ordinance,
the enactments mentioned in the Schedule shall, if and so far as applicable to
such institution, immediately before coming into force of this Ordinance,
continue to apply thereto.

Provincialisation of primary education

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER I.‑PRELIMINARY
4. Provincialisation of primary education.‑As from the date
of enforcement of this Ordinance in any area, in this Chapter referred to as
the said date, primary education shall, notwithstanding anything contained in
any other law for the time being in force in that area, be under the control of
Government, and all rights, authority and jurisdiction vested in or exercised
by a local council in respect of primary education in primary schools in that
area immediately before the said date, shall‑-
(i) except in so far as may be
otherwise provided by or under this Ordinance or as may be otherwise directed
by Government, cease to vest in and be
exercisable by the local council; and
(ii) vest in and be exercisable
by Government in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance.

Power to except any institution in a local area

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER I.‑PRELIMINARY
5. Power to except any institution in a local area.‑Notwithstanding
anything contained in section 4, Government may, by notification In the
official Gazette, except from the operation of the provisions of section 4,
such educational institutions in a local area as may be specified.

Transfer of staff and property on provincialisation

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER I.‑PRELIMINARY
6. Transfer of staff and property
on provinciallsation.‑As from the said date, subject to the provisions of
section 5‑
(a) all properties and assets vested In a local council for the
purposes of primary education shall vest in Government for the purposes of
primary education ;
(b) all teachers and other staff employed by a local council in
connec tion with primary education shall stand transferred for service to and
be employed by Government on such terms and conditions including the terms
regarding pay, pension and contribution to Provident Fund, as the Govern ment
may determine; provided that such terms and conditions shall not be less
favourable than the terms and conditions on which such persons were employed by
the local council, and ;
(c) all rights, liabilities and
obligations of the local council, relating to properties and assets or to
contracts, debts or payments or receipts of money, accrued or incurred
immediately before the said date shall become the rights, liabilities and
obligations of Government.

District primary education committee

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER II‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION COMMITTEE
7. District primary Education Committee.‑(1) As soon as may be,
there shall be constituted in every District, District Primary Education
Committee, in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance.
(i) Every District Primary
Education Committee shall be a body corporate, having perpetual succession and
a common seal, and shall by its name sue and be sued.
(3) Every District Primary Education
Committee, shall be known by the name of the District concerned.

Constitution of the district primary education committee

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER II‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION COMMITTEE
8. Constitution of the District Primary Education
Committee.‑(I) A District Primary Education Committee, shall consist of‑
(a) the Collector of the
district ;
(b) the District Inspector of
Schools ;
(c) the District Inspectress of
Schools ; and
(d) three members, hereinafter
referred to as appointed members, to be appointed by the Commissioner, at least
two of whom shall be from among the elected members of the local councils, in
the District.
(2) (a) The term of office of
an appointed member shall be five years.
(b) An appointed member may
resign his office by tendering his resigna tion to the Collector and the seat
of such member shall become vacant when the resignation is accepted by the
Commissioner.
(c) The Commissioner may, by an
order in writing and for reasons to be specified, remove any appointed member
from his office and thereupon the seat of such member shall become vacant.
(d) If the seat of an appointed
member becomes vacant, a new member shall be appointed by the Commissioner and
such member .hall hold office, for the full term of five years.
(3) Every appointment,
resignation or removal of a member shall be notified by the Commissioner in the
official Gazette.
(4) The Collector shall ex‑officio
be the Chairman of the District Primary Education Committee.
(5) The District Inspector of
Schools shall ex‑officio be the Secretary of the District Primary
Education Committee.

Functions of the district primary education committee

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER II‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION COMMITTEE
9. Functions of the District
Primary Education Committee.‑(1)
Subject to rules and such directions as Government may from time to time
give, a District Primary Education Committee shall advise, aid and assist
Government in the‑
(a) provision and maintenance
of Government primary schools;
(b) undertaking of educational
surveys, framing of educational plans and enforcement thereof ; and
(c) adoption of such other
measures as may be necessary for the promotion of primary education.
(2) If a local council fails to
provide necessary facilities for primary education, the District Primary
Education Committee shall move the Controlling Authority concerned to direct
the local council to fulfil its obligations.

Conduct of business

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER II‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION COMMITTEE
10. Conduct of business.‑(1) The business of
the District Primary Education Committee shall be conducted at its meetings in
such manner as may be prescribed.
(2) Save as otherwise provided in the rules, the executive powers
of a District Primary Education Committee shall vest In and be exercised by‑
(a) in the case of boys'
schools, the District Inspector of Schools ;
(b) in the case of girls' schools, the District Inspectress of
Schools.
(3) Subject to rules, the
executive powers of a District Primary Educa tion Committee shall extend to the‑
(a) conduct of day‑to‑day
administration ;
(b) general superintendence and
inspection of Government primary schools ;
(c) appointment of teachers and
other staff for Government primary schools, their promotion, transfer,
punishment and removal ; and
(d) incurring of expenditure on any one item up to such amount as
may be prescribed, or in the absence of rules, as may be specified by the
District Primary Education Committee.

Appeals

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER II‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION COMMITTEE
11. Appeals.‑Any person
aggrieved by an order passed by the District Inspector of Schools or the
District Inspectress of Schools, in exercise of the executive powers under
subsections (2) and (3) of section 10, may prefer an appeal to the District
Primary Education Committee within thirty days of such order, and thereupon the
:District Primary Education Committee may confirm, modify or set aside the
order, or remand the case for recon sideration by the District Inspector of
Schools, or the District Inspectress of Schools, as the case may be.

Records reports and returns

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER II‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION COMMITTEE
12. Records reports and returns..‑A District Primary
Education Committee shall maintain such record of its working and prepare and
publish such periodical reports and returns as may be prescribed.

Staff

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER II‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION COMMITTEE
13. Staff.‑(i) A District Primary Education Committee may
from time to time, with the previous sanction of Government, draw up an establishment
schedule specifying the establishment to be entertained for the purposes of
primary education in Government primary schools in the District.
(2) No appointment shall be
made against a post not provided for in the establishment schedule except with
the previous sanction of Government.
(3) Government may prescribe‑--
(a) the conditions of service of persons employed for the purposes
of primary education In Government primary schools ;
(b) the grades of pay of such persons;
(c) the principles to be
followed in making appointments, promotions and transfers of such persons ;
(d) the method of holding
enquiries in cases where disciplinary action Is proposed to be taken against
such persons, the penalties that may be imposed, and the manner of preferring
appeals against order imposing penal ties ; and
(e) other matters necessary for efficient discharge by such persons
of their duties.
(4) Save as otherwise provided
by or under this Ordinance, all persons employed in a District for the purposes
of primary education shall be Government servants.

District primary education fund

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER III.‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION FUND
14. District Primary Education Fund.‑In every District, for
the purposes of primary education, there shall be a Fund which shall be known
as the District Primary Education Fund.
(2) To the credit of the
District Primary Education Fund shall be placed‑--
(a) the proceeds of all taxes, rates, tolls, cesses and fees levied
in the District by Government or by the District Council under directions of
Govern ment for the purposes of primary education ;
(b) such share of the proceeds of the local rate levied in the
District as may be specified by Government from time to time ;
(c) all grants made by
Government for the purposes of primary edu cation In Government primary schools
in the District ;
(d) all sums contributed by
local councils, individuals, institutions and other bodies for the purposes of
primary education In Government primary schools ;
(e) all rents and profits payable or accruing to the District
Primary Education Committee from the property vested in Government for the
purposes of primary education ;
(f ) all receipts accruing from the trust placed at the disposal of
the District Primary Education Committee for the purposes of primary education
; and
(g) proceeds from such sources
of income as Government may direct to be placed at the disposal of the District
Primary Education Committee.
(3) The moneys credited to a
District Primary Education Fund shall be kept in a Government treasury, or in a
bank transacting the business of a Government treasury, or in such other manner
as may be specified by Government from time to time.
(4) The money from time to time
credited to the District Primary Education Fund shall be applied for the
following purposes :‑
(a) the payment of salaries and allowances to the persons employed
for the purposes of primary education in Government primary schools in the
District ;
(b) the fulfilment of any obligation, and the discharge of any
duty, imposed on the District Primary Education Committee by or under this
Ordinance ; and
(c) the meeting of any
expenditure declared by Government to be an appropriate charge on the District
Primary Education Fund.

Budget accounts and audit

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER III.‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION FUND
15. Budget, accounts and audit.‑(1) A District Primary
Education Committee shall, in the prescribed manner, prepare and sanction,
before the commencement of each financial year, hereinafter referred to as the
budget, and forward copies thereof to the District Council, Divisional Council,
Provincial Primary Education Committee and Government.
(2) Government may, on the
representation of the District Council, or Divisional Council, or Provincial
Primary education Committee or otherwise, amend or modify the budget of a
District Primary Education Committee in such manner as may be specified.
(3) Accounts of the District
Primary Education Fund shall be kept in such manner and form as may be
prescribed.
(4) An annual statement of the
accounts shall be prepared after the close of each financial year and copies
thereof shall be forwarded to the District Council, Divisional Council;
Provincial Primary Education Committee and Government.
(5) The accounts of a District
Primary Education Committee shall be audited in such manner, after such
intervals, and by such authority as may be prescribed.

District primary education development plan

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER III.‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION FUND
16 District Primary Education Development Plan.‑(1) A District
Primary Education Committee shall prepare development plans for primary education
in the District for such periods and in such manner as may be specified by
Government.
(2) A District Primary
Education Development Plan shall provide for‑
(a) the promotion, improvement
and development of primary education In the District ;
(b) the manner in which the
plan shall be financed, executed, implemen ted and supervised ; and
(c) such other matters as may
be specified by Government.
(3) The District Primary
Education Committee small submit the plan prepared under the preceding subsection
to Government and shall forward copies hereof to the District Council,
Divisional Council and the Provincial Primary Education Committee.
(4) Government may reject the
plan submitted to it under subsection (3) or sanction it without modification
or subject to such modifications as may be specified or may return it to the
District Primary Education Committee for reconsideration.
(5) The District Primary
Education Committee shall implement the plan as finally sanctioned by
Government.

Compulsory primary education

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER III.‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION FUND
17. Compulsory primary
education.‑(I) Government may, by means of a scheme containing the
prescribed particulars, introduce compulsory primary education in any District
or any part thereof.
(2) In an area of compulsion
the parent of a child residing within such area shall, except in the case of a
reasonable excuse, cause the child to attend a recognised school until the
child has completed the primary education course.
(3) A scheme made under
subsection (1) shall be notified in the official Gazette.
(4) Government may, from time
to time, amend, vary or modify any scheme made under subsection (1).
(5) Where compulsory education
has been introduced in any area under any enactment specified in the Schedule,
it shall, subject to such modifications as may be made by Government, be
continued and be deemed to have been introduced under this Ordinance.

Reasonable excuse for non-attendance

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER III.‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION FUND
18. Reasonable excuse for non‑attendance.‑"Reasonable
excuse" for the purposes of subsection (2) of section 17 shall include any
of the following cases :‑
(a) where the child is
prevented from attending school by sickness, Infirmity or other unavoidable
cause ;
(6) where the child is
receiving, otherwise than in a recognised school, Instruction which, in the
opinion of the District Inspector of Schools In the case of a boy, and the
District Inspectress of Schools, in the case of a girl, is efficient ;
(c) where there is no
recognised school within a distance to be fixed by Government and measured
according to the nearest route, from the residence of the child ;
(d) where after due
application, admission to a recognised school has been refused to the child and
there is no other recognised school to which he can be admitted within the
distance fixed under clause (c) until such time as the parent is informed that
the child can be admitted ;
(e) where the District
Inspector of Schools In the case of a boy, or the District Inspectress of
Schools In the case of a girl, is satisfied that by reason of the child's
mental incapacity, it is not desirable that the child should be compelled to
prosecute his or her studies further.

School attendance authority

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER III.‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION FUND
19. School Attendance
Authority.‑(1) In a Cantonment, Municipality, Town or Union, the
Cantonment Board, Municipal Committee, Town Committee, Union Council or Union
Committee, as the case may be, shall be the School Attendance Authority for the
purposes of this Ordinance.
(2) A School Attendance
Authority shall ensure that every child required to attend a recognised school
under this Ordinance attends a recognised school and for this purpose shall
take such steps as may be considered necessary by the Authority, or may be
specified by Government.
(3) Where a School Attendance
Authority is satisfied that a parent who Is required under this Ordinance to
cause a child to attend a recognised school, has failed to do so, the
Authority, after giving the parent an oppor tunity of being heard and after
such inquiry as it considers necessary, may pass an order directing the parent
to cause such child to attend a recognised school on and from a date which
shall be specified in the order.

Offences

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER III.‑DISTRICT
PRIMARY EDUCATION FUND
20. Offences.‑(1) Any
parent who fails to comply with an order issued under subsection (3) of section
19 shall, on conviction before a Magistrate, be punishable with fine which may
extend to fifty rupees and with further fine which may extend to five rupees
for every day after the conviction for which the failure continues.
(2) Any person who, after
receiving due warning from the School Attendance Authority continues to employ
a child required under this Ordinance to attend a recognised school, whether on
remuneration or other wise, shall on conviction before a Magistrate be
punishable with fine which may extend to fifty rupees and with a further fine
which may extend to five rupees for every day after the conviction for which
the non‑attendance at a recognised school continues.
(3) No Court shall take
cognizance of any offence under this section except on a complaint in writing
made by the Chairman of the School Attendance Authority.
(4) (a) The School Attendance
Authority may compound any offence punishable under this section ;
(b) Any amount realised by the
School Attendance Authority on composition under subsection (1) shall be
credited to the funds of the Can tonment Board, Municipal Committee or the
local council concerned.

sections.description:
Provincial primary education committee

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER V‑GENERAL
21. Provincial Primary
Education Committee.‑.(1) As soon as may be, there shall be established a
Committee to be known as the Provincial Primary Education Committee.
(2) The Provincial Primary
Education Committee shall consist of such members as may be appointed by
Government.
(3) The functions of the
Provincial Primary Education Committee shall be‑
(a) to advise Government on
matters pertaining to primary education and its promotion and development in
the Province or any part thereof ;
(b) to assess the finances
required for the promotion and development of primary education in the Province
or any part thereof ;
(c) to suggest ways and means
for financing primary education, including the levy of education cess ; and
(d) such other functions as may
be specified by Government.

Functions of district and divisional council

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER V‑GENERAL
22. Functions of District and Divisional Councils.‑(I) A District
Council may from time to time review generally the progress in primary
education in the District and may recommend to Government and the District
Primary Education Committee such proposals for the promotion of primary
education in the District as may be necessary.
(2) A Divisional Council may
from time to time review generally the progress in primary education in the
Division and may recommend to Government such proposals for the promotion of
primary education in the Division as may be necessary.

Proposals for new primary schools

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER V‑GENERAL
23. Proposals for new primary schools.‑A proposal
formulated by the District Primary Education Committee for the location of a
new primary school shall be subject to the concurrence‑--
(a) in case the school is to be located in a municipality, of the
Municipal Committee; and
(b) in any other case, of the District Council.

Provisions of new school buildings and equipment

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER V‑GENERAL
24. Provision of new school buildings and equipment.‑(1) In a munici pality, the Municipal Committee,
in a Town, the Town Committee, and in a Union in rural area, the Union Council
shall, as far as possible, be responsible for the provision of new school
building along with the requisite equipment of such design and standard as may
be specified by Government from time to time.
(2) A building for a primary
school located in a municipality, Town or Union in a rural area shall, as far
as possible, be maintained by the Municipal Committee, the Town Committee or
the Union Council, as the case may be, to the satisfaction of the District
Primary Education Committee.

Visitation

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER V‑GENERAL
25. Visitation.‑A member
of a local council may visit any primary school in the local area and record
his remarks in the visitors book main tained in the primary school.

Government to make rules

ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
ORDINANCE XXIX OF 1962
WEST PAKISTAN PRIMARY EDUCATION
ORDINANCE, 1962
CHAPTER V‑GENERAL
26. (1) Government may make
rules to carry out the purposes of the Ordinance.
(2) All rules made under
subsection (1) shall be notified in the official Gazette.
